summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Asteria Cloud to explore a reseller / co-hosting partnership for GPU-based inference. Discussed integration patterns (hosted API, dedicated pools, private VPC), security and compliance needs, initial benchmarking plan, and next steps for a technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-19 15:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Attendees: Lena M., Arjun P., Maya C. (Redwood) -- Emilia R., Derek W., Sara K., Tom A. (Asteria)

00:00 Lena Morales: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood inference, i'm the account lead, arjun is our se and maya from solutions will help with partner ops. how are you all?
00:08 Emilia Ross: hey lena -- good thanks, excited to chat. we've been looking at inference partners to expand our marketplace and also offer co-managed GPU capacity.
00:18 Derek Wu: yea, hi, derek here. quick context, asteria runs regional cloud zones in eu/us/apac, we do bare-metal racks with nvidia-ish hardware, and want to explore serving partners who can plug into our hosting and also potentially resell a managed inference offering.
00:33 Arjun Patel: great -- that's exactly the pattern some of our partners take. quick agenda: intro + goals, current infra and constraints, security/compliance, integration models (hosted/dedicated/private), perf/cost tradeoffs, next steps. sound good?
00:45 Sara Kline: yep.

01:00 Lena Morales: can you walk through asteria's typical customer -- like who buys capacity from you, and what SLAs or features drive deals?
01:10 Derek Wu: mostly ai startups and enterprise platform teams. they want predictable latency and cost, some need vpc-level isolation, some need air-gapped/offline installs for regulated industries. SLA expectations vary -- 99.9 for premium, lower for self-serve.
01:25 Lena Morales: ok, good. on the redwood side we offer three modes -- Redwood API hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved gpu pools you can map to partner POPs) and Redwood Private (vpc or on-prem control plane). partners often want a combination: a co-branded hosted route plus an optional private offering for large customers.
01:45 Tom Alvarez: security is big for us -- can you describe what you do for key management and logging? specifically around kms/hsm and audit logs.
01:55 Arjun Patel: sure -- we support customer-managed KMS keys for Private and Dedicated, integrate with HSMs for on-prem, and have per-request audit logs plus token-level cost traces in the console. we'll share SOC 2 docs. (slight pause) note: sometimes our transcript tool writes K V cache as K V cash in docs, so apologies if you see odd wording.
02:18 Emilia Ross: haha no worries. on integration -- are you thinking partners would run a control plane with you or just the runtime?
02:25 Maya Chen: typically partner models vary -- for reseller/co-host we can offer a managed control plane with region-specific routing, or give partners the private deployment package so they run their own control plane and just use our model catalog and runtime. both have tradeoffs on upgrades and support.
02:40 Derek Wu: for our customers we need data residency controls, and many ask for SSO/SAML + RBAC. can you support per-tenant encryption and audit retention policies?
02:52 Arjun Patel: yes -- per-tenant keys and configurable retention windows are supported on Private; Dedicated has logical isolation and we can instrument longer audit retention as an add-on. SSO and SCIM for user provisioning is standard.
03:08 Sara Kline: on the perf side, what kind of throughput/latency should we expect if we colocate with your dedicated pools? our customers push concurrent chat workloads with 1-2k RPS spikes.
03:20 Arjun Patel: performance depends on model family, quantization and batching; in our benchmarks a mid-sized model served on a 1U A100 type yields X latencies -- sorry, bad audio earlier, meant low 90ms p95 for short prompts with optimized kernels. for batched generation throughput we use continuous batching and KV cache to amortize costs.
03:42 Derek Wu: can we run a joint benchmark with our workload?
03:44 Lena Morales: absolutely. proposed plan: share a sample prompt set and traffic shape, we spin up a dedicated pool in your POP or run a hosted variant routed to your region, run 3 days of tests, and share a benchmark report. we'll include cost-per-token breakdown and p95 latency.
04:00 Emilia Ross: sounds reasonable. what are the integration touchpoints -- is there an api?
04:06 Maya Chen: we have a simple REST/SDK api for generation and embeddings; plus model catalog versioning, streaming, and function-calling primitives. for partners we expose routing hooks so you can enforce region routing and quota. we'll share docs link in the follow-up.
04:24 Tom Alvarez: legal/procurement -- how do partners handle revenue share and support SLAs? any templates?
04:30 Lena Morales: we have standard partner agreements and can do reseller revenue splits. support SLAs are configurable; for dedicated/reserved customers we typically sign an enterprise SOW with support tiers. i'll share templates and a draft MSA.
04:42 Derek Wu: curious of roadmap -- do you plan more hardware support beyond nvidia? our roadmap includes amd/arm nodes.
04:50 Arjun Patel: yes, we are hardware agnostic in principle -- runtime has kernel selection and backends for different accelerators; we do active work on amd support and quantization-friendly kernels for arm/alae. some internal names might come out wrong in this transcript, but we'll provide the real compatibility matrix.
05:05 Sara Kline: any concerns about multi-tenancy if we host workloads for different customers; we need strong isolation and per-tenant metrics.
05:12 Arjun Patel: with Dedicated you get logical isolation, and with Private you can run a separate control plane per customer. we also support network policies, node taints and hardware affinity so you can isolate customers at rack level.
05:25 Lena Morales: couple of commercial questions that often come up -- cost models, burst capacity, and overprovision. do you sell committed rack capacity to customers today?
05:35 Derek Wu: yes some customers buy reserved racks, others prefer on-demand. we'd like to offer combined reserved + burst options.
05:40 Lena Morales: we can support reserved capacity for predictable throughput and autoscaling for bursts; Redwood Optimize can help with batching and quantization suggestions to lower unit costs.
05:50 Emilia Ross: ok great. curious if you have references for partners with similar reseller models?
05:54 Maya Chen: yes -- we have a couple of partners in eu who run co-hosted stacks; i'll put you in touch after the call.
06:05 Derek Wu: security checklist -- SOC2, ISO, encryption at rest/in transit, penetration test results, vulnerability triage process, and PCI? some clients also ask for specific compliance.
06:20 Lena Morales: we'll send SOC 2, pen test summary, and our vulnerability policy. for regulated customers we recommend private deployment with customer-managed KMS.
06:28 Tom Alvarez: thanks. on timelines -- if we wanted to pilot in q3, what's a realistic ramp?
06:32 Lena Morales: pilot could start in 4-6 weeks after we share requirements and infra access; full production depends on integration depth, typically 8-12 weeks with a canary rollout.
06:42 Arjun Patel: technical deep dive items: network diagram, packet capture requirements, quantized model artifacts, sample prompt corpus, and traffic profile. please share those and we'll scope the test.
06:56 Emilia Ross: we'll gather that. also can you advise on pricing granularity -- token vs inference call vs throughput?
07:04 Lena Morales: for hosted it's token-based; for dedicated/reserved it's a combination of committed capacity + per-request overage; we can propose reseller-friendly pricing in the next doc.
07:16 Derek Wu: vendor questions -- do you integrate with monitoring stacks like datadog, prometheus, and do you export traces?
07:22 Arjun Patel: yes we have metrics and tracing hooks, datadog integrations, prometheus exporters, and we expose per-route traces and logs to your observability stack.
07:35 Sara Kline: quick tech nit -- what about model updates / rollouts, can partners pin versions? we need stable model behavior for enterprise customers.
07:42 Maya Chen: partners can pin model versions and do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to older variants if regressions detected. Redwood also ties regressions to eval prompt sets.
07:56 Lena Morales: ok recap and next steps: lena to send partner one-pager, deck, security docs; arjun to draft config recommendations and test plan; asteria to share SOC2 excerpt, network diagram and sample prompts; agree on benchmarking week of 6/29.
08:15 Emilia Ross: yep we'll aim to have docs by 6/24 and confirm benchmarking slot.
08:22 Lena Morales: perfect. closing -- thanks everyone, i'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
08:30 Derek Wu: thanks all.

Notes: audio has a few mis-transcribed acronyms (K V cache -> K V cash) and occasionally speaker labels collapsed. Shared artifacts: partner-deck.pdf (link), redwood-benchmark-template.xlsx (link), redwood-security-SOC2.pdf (link).

End of transcript.
